To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the elicitor-induced formation of PA and DGPA in tomato cells is mediated primarily by DAG kinase; (2) the elicitor treatment activates the turnover of phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylinisitol-4-phosphate; and (3) the elicitor-mediated accumulation of DGPP is correlated with the induction of defense responses.
1) Elicitors induce the accumulation of phosphatidate (PA) and diacylgycerol pyrophosphate in cultured tomato cells.
1) Elicitation of suspension cultured tomato cells triggers the rapid accumulation of PA and DAGPP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the generation of PA and DG.
the elucidation of signaling events triggered by elicitors in tomato cells.
the identification and quantification of lipid mediators of plant defense signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elicitor-induced production of PA and DG is not mediated via phospholipase A, but by phospholipaseC and DAG kinase.
PA is formed by DAG kinase and that DGPP is formed by the phosphorylation of PA.
PA is a secondary product of elicitor-induced signaling in tomato cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
elicitor treatment triggers rapid and transient accumulation of PA in tomato cells, which is mainly produced by DAG kinase.
PA and DGPP are elicitor-responsive lipid molecules in plant cells and that they are formed by a pathway involving DAG kinase.

elicitors induce the rapid formation of phosphatidylinositide-derived phosphatidic acids and diacylglyceryl pyrophosphates in tomato suspension cells, and that these molecules may act as second messengers to mediate plant defense signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of PA and DGPA can be triggered in suspension-cultures of tomato cells by the treatment with general elicitors.
the activation of phosphatidate phosphatase, which degrades PA to DAG, may be an important regulatory step in the control of PA and DG signaling in plants.
PA and DGPP can be rapidly formed in plant cells upon elicitor treatment, and that the main source of PA is from DAG kinase.
